transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is that my shoulders and my neck just stay clenched all day long. It's like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. And by the time evening rolls around, my jaw aches so badly I can hardly even enjoy playing my guitar anymore. I just can't seem to untense my muscles.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate reason to?

Yes, all the time. It's like my mind just won't stop circling. I worry about whether I'll ever get hired again, or if I've somehow ruined my reputation with the parents. I think about whether retirement is just slipping away from me. It gets to the point where I even worry that a small mistake during a story-time activity means I shouldn't be trusted with children anymore. There's not always a direct reason for it, but the thoughts are just constantly there.
Did these worries start after a specific stressful event?
Yes, actually. This whole thing started about a year and two months ago, right after I was fired from the preschool. That was definitely the event that set it all off.
Are your worries mostly just about losing that preschool job, or do they regularly spread to lots of other parts of your life too?

They definitely spread to a lot of other things. Like I mentioned before, it's not just about losing the job itself. My mind just keeps circling. I worry about whether I'll ever get hired again, but then it spirals into worrying if I've ruined my reputation with the parents in the community. Then I start stressing about my finances and whether retirement is just slipping away from me entirely. And it even gets down to the little things, like I'll obsess over whether a small mistake I made during a story-time activity in the past means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. It just bounces from one thing to the next.
When the worrying starts, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yes, it really is. I try to stop it—I'll tell myself to just make a list, or I'll try to pray, or go out and weed the garden, just to focus on the next practical step. But it doesn't really work. One worry just hands off to another, and before I know it, I've lost half the afternoon just sitting there spinning my wheels.
Have you been feeling this worried most days for at least six months?

Yes, definitely. Like I mentioned a minute ago, this has been going on for about a year and two months now, ever since I was fired from the preschool. And it really is most days... honestly, it feels like every single day. So yes, it's been well over six months.
Do your worries still feel mainly centered on being fired from the preschool?

Well, like I was saying earlier, it definitely started with being fired. That was the... the trigger, I guess. But at this point, no, I wouldn't say it's mainly centered on just that anymore. It's really branched out. 

The preschool job is what set it off fourteen months ago, but now it's my finances, my retirement, what the community thinks of me... it just latches onto everything else now. So it might have started with the job, but it's definitely not just about that anymore.
